subject: pirate perch
title: Frogs Avoid 10 Kinds of Fish by Smell. This One Sneaks Right Past

scenes.text: Frogs avoid ponds with fish. This fish is the exception.
Tree frogs and water beetles sniff out predatory fish and settle somewhere else.
Researchers hid eleven fish species behind screens in test ponds. Prey avoided every one but one.
Ponds with the pirate perch filled up almost as if no fish were there.
The likely reason: it masks its own scent, so prey can't smell it coming.
And it hides one more oddity. As it grows, its anus moves forward to its throat.

description:
Frogs and water beetles avoid ponds that smell of fish, except ponds holding the pirate perch.
In a study published in The American Naturalist, prey avoided all eleven fish species tested except this one, which seems to mask its scent.
What other animal do you think hides by smell?
first_comment: The pirate perch is only about four to five inches long and lives in swamps and slow streams in the eastern US. Ever seen one?
